topic.subject: science
topic.title: Fibres and plastics
topic.scope: natural and synthetic fibres, nylon, polyester, thermoplastics and thermosetting plastics, plastics and environment

misconceptions.statement: Cotton is a synthetic fibre because it is processed in large machines in factories.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate 'industrial processing' with 'synthetic' or 'man-made'.
misconceptions.fix: Cotton is natural because the raw material is obtained directly from the cotton plant, regardless of how it is spun.

probe.question: If a factory spins cotton into a shirt, does the fibre become synthetic?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because it was made by machines.

misconceptions.root_belief: industrial processing makes a substance synthetic

misconceptions.statement: Synthetic fibres are made of chemicals, but natural fibres are chemical-free.
misconceptions.why: In everyday language, 'chemicals' is used as a synonym for 'artificial' or 'toxic'.
misconceptions.fix: All matter, including natural fibres like cotton (cellulose), is made of chemical substances.

probe.question: Is the cellulose in a cotton plant a chemical?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it is natural, so it has no chemicals.

misconceptions.root_belief: natural things do not contain chemicals

misconceptions.statement: Rayon is a fully natural fibre because it is made from wood pulp.
misconceptions.why: Students focus on the biological origin of the raw material and ignore the chemical treatment.
misconceptions.fix: Rayon is semi-synthetic; although it comes from wood pulp, it requires extensive chemical processing to become a fibre.

probe.question: Why is Rayon called 'artificial silk' if it comes from wood?
probe.wrong_answer: Because wood is natural, so the silk it makes is natural.

misconceptions.root_belief: origin of raw material determines final classification

misconceptions.statement: Natural fibres like silk are always stronger than synthetic fibres like nylon.
misconceptions.why: There is an intuitive belief that nature's designs are superior in strength to man-made ones.
misconceptions.fix: A nylon thread is actually stronger than a steel wire of the same thickness.

probe.question: Which is stronger: a nylon thread or a cotton thread of the same thickness?

misconceptions.root_belief: natural materials are inherently superior to artificial ones

misconceptions.statement: All plastics can be melted and reshaped multiple times.
misconceptions.why: Students generalize their experience with plastic bottles and bags to all plastic items.
misconceptions.fix: Only thermoplastics can be melted and reshaped; thermosetting plastics stay hard once set.

probe.question: Can you melt an old electric switch to make a plastic toy?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, all plastic melts when heated.

misconceptions.root_belief: members of a category share all properties

misconceptions.statement: Thermosetting plastics like Bakelite are actually metals because they are hard and don't melt.
misconceptions.why: Students associate hardness and heat resistance exclusively with metals.
misconceptions.fix: Bakelite is a plastic with a cross-linked polymer structure that prevents it from softening on heating.

probe.question: Why doesn't a pressure cooker handle melt on the stove?
probe.wrong_answer: Because it is made of a black metal.

misconceptions.statement: If you bury plastic in the soil for many years, it will eventually turn into compost.
misconceptions.why: Students apply the logic of biological decay (like food or paper) to all buried objects.
misconceptions.fix: Plastics are non-biodegradable; microorganisms cannot break down their polymer chains, so they persist for centuries.

probe.question: What happens to a plastic bag buried in the ground for 100 years?
probe.wrong_answer: It will rot and become part of the soil.

misconceptions.root_belief: all things from the earth return to the earth

misconceptions.statement: Burning plastic is a good way to get rid of it because it disappears.
misconceptions.why: Visible disappearance of the solid object is equated with the removal of the problem.
misconceptions.fix: Burning plastic releases toxic fumes into the atmosphere and does not 'destroy' the matter safely.

probe.question: Is burning plastic better for the environment than burying it?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because burning makes it go away completely.

misconceptions.root_belief: what you cannot see does not exist

misconceptions.statement: A polymer is a single large atom.
misconceptions.why: Confusion between the scale of atoms, molecules, and macroscopic objects.
misconceptions.fix: A polymer is a very large molecule made of many small repeating units called monomers.

probe.question: What is a polymer made of?
probe.wrong_answer: It is one giant atom of plastic.

misconceptions.root_belief: small particles are all the same size

misconceptions.statement: Recycling is the only 'R' that matters for saving the environment from plastic.
misconceptions.why: Recycling is the most publicized 'R' in media and school posters.
misconceptions.fix: Reducing and Refusing are more effective than recycling, as recycling also requires energy and resources.

probe.question: If we recycle all our plastic, have we solved the plastic problem?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, recycling is the complete solution.

misconceptions.root_belief: one solution fixes the whole problem

misconceptions.statement: Polyester is better for summer because it is thin and light.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the weight of the fabric with its ability to absorb sweat and allow air circulation.
misconceptions.fix: Polyester absorbs very little water and traps heat, making it uncomfortable in hot, humid weather compared to cotton.

probe.question: Why do we prefer cotton clothes in summer over polyester?
probe.wrong_answer: We don't; polyester is lighter so it must be cooler.

misconceptions.statement: Biodegradable materials like paper never cause any environmental pollution.
misconceptions.why: The term 'biodegradable' is often perceived as 'perfectly safe' in all contexts.
misconceptions.fix: Even biodegradable waste can cause pollution (like methane in landfills) if not managed properly.

probe.question: Can throwing too much paper in a river be harmful?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because paper is biodegradable and will just disappear.

misconceptions.root_belief: good qualities apply in all situations
